title: Exa MCP password and API key printed in plaintext by claude_code role
description: Discovered during ansible-all-my-things-pjoh (T011a validation, branch 014-desktop-profile): roles/claude_code/tasks/install-addons.yml tasks 'Check if exa MCP server is already configured' (line 265) and 'Configure exa MCP server' (line 277) loop over desktop_users, whose items contain plaintext password and exa_api_key fields. Neither task sets no_log: true, so every ansible-playbook run that hits this role prints the full item dict — including the real password and exa_api_key — to the console/log via Ansible's default loop-item echo. Confirmed live: a configure-profile.yml run against host romulus printed both secrets in full in the terminal output. Fix: add no_log: true to both tasks.
close_reason: Fixed in 40a54bc (no_log: true on both exa MCP tasks); verified live on host romulus — both tasks now show (censored due to no_log) instead of plaintext password/exa_api_key. Secrets rotated by user.

title: claude_code's own background auto-updater can silently drift the pinned version
description:
Researched via official docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/setup): native/npm Claude Code installs auto-update in the background by default (checks on startup + periodically, downloads+installs, takes effect next launch). Only Homebrew/WinGet/apt/dnf/apk installs do NOT auto-update by default -- that's a property of the install method.

roles/claude_code/tasks/install-claude-code.yml downloads the binary directly via get_url (ansible-all-my-things-jvs4.1.14.1), bypassing the native installer's versioned-directory+shim layout (~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version>/ + a ~/.local/bin/claude pointer) but NOT bypassing the binary's own baked-in auto-update behavior. Nothing currently disables it. This means the actually-running claude version on a host can silently drift away from the pinned claude_code_version in roles/claude_code/defaults/main.yml the next time the user launches claude -- defeating the explicit-pin-controlled-only-by-perform-updates.yml model this entire migration (m0av.1-4, jvs4.1.14.1) establishes for every other tool (rtk, beads, nodejs all have no self-update mechanism; claude_code uniquely does, and nothing currently constrains it).

FIX (agreed with reviewer): set BOTH env vars in settings.json to fully block every update path:
- DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 (stops the background update check)
- DISABLE_UPDATES=1 (also blocks manual 'claude update'/'claude install', the stronger guarantee)

Implementation: add both keys to the jq merge in roles/claude_code/tasks/configure.yml:34 (the .env = (.env // {} | . + {...}) merge that already sets CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS/CLAUDE_CODE_SPAWN_BACKEND), and to verify.yml's settings.json assertions alongside the existing agent-team keys check. Also update docs (roles/claude_code/README.md and/or DESIGN.md) to document why auto-update is disabled -- ties the pin model together for a future reader who might otherwise wonder why these two env vars are set.
close_reason: Human-reviewed and accepted (gate ansible-all-my-things-9hzb)

title: bd list --all runaway: unbounded output (5.6GB), 100% CPU, SIGKILL (137)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (corrected): `bd list --all` itself enters an unbounded output loop in this repo (~350 issues). It is NOT the grep / pipe. Confirmed across two crashes: 1. Session 1: `bd list --all 2>&1 | grep -i "phase 6|legacy|retire"` — hung 100% CPU, minutes, manual session kill. 2. Session 2: `bd list --all > file 2>&1` (NO grep, NO live pipe consumer, plain file redirect) — also hung 100% CPU and was SIGKILLed. Exit code 137 = 128+9 = SIGKILL (OOM-killer / watchdog killing a runaway process). EVIDENCE: the partial redirect file reached 5,622,719,849 bytes (5.6 GB) before the kill. bd emitted 5.6GB of output for ~350 issues = unbounded/looping output generation. This fills RAM and disk, pegs CPU, and triggers SIGKILL. The earlier 'pipe-to-grep / SIGPIPE' hypothesis is WRONG — grep is exonerated; the redirect-to-file form reproduces identically. IMPACT: crashes the agent VM (the 5.6GB file also nearly filled the 17G disk). Reproducible. Must never run `bd list --all` in this repo. WORKAROUND (automated as of 2026-06-27): three-layer guard now in place: 1. AGENTS.md prohibition with safe alternatives documented 2. Claude Code PreToolUse Bash hook in .claude/settings.json blocks the command with an actionable error message 3. claude_code Ansible role (configure.yml) idempotently merges the hook into settings.json — survives VM deletion/restore For bulk reads use .beads/issues.jsonl directly (grep/jq). For live queries: `bd ready`, `bd list --status `, `bd show `, `bd list --priority

`. UPSTREAM: bd v1.0.4 bug needs to be filed with upstream (user action item — requires capturing bd version and DB size outside the agent VM).
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract nerd font install from tmux role into dedicated role
description:
WHY: The tmux role installs an iconic Nerd Font gated by tmux_install_iconic_font (roles/tmux/defaults/main.yml). This second responsibility violates Principle II (single responsibility) and is the root cause of the desktop-profile conflict recorded in feat.create-destroy-vm FINDINGS.md item 2: legacy configure-linux-roles.yml sets tmux_install_iconic_font: true as a play-var, which the planned Phase 5a verbatim import would carry into a shared role list and silently apply to basic-profile hosts. A Nerd Font only renders where a desktop renders glyphs locally (XFCE/XRDP); it is dead weight on headless servers. Extracting it removes the flag, kills the conflict at the source, and aligns font ownership with the desktop profile.

WHAT:
- New role (e.g. nerd_font): defaults (font version + arch map), tasks from roles/tmux/tasks/install-font.yml, meta, molecule/default scenario (port today's roles/tmux/molecule/with-font as the default scenario).
- tmux role: remove install-font.yml; remove tmux_font_version and tmux_install_iconic_font from defaults/main.yml; remove the install-font import + when from tasks/main.yml; delete molecule/with-font; drop the font-absent assertions from molecule/default/verify.yml; fix meta/main.yml description.
- version-update mechanism: re-point the ryanoasis/nerd-fonts fetch/query/report/update wiring from the tmux defaults path to the new role defaults path (playbooks/update-versions/query-versions.yml + perform-updates.yml). github_repo stays ryanoasis/nerd-fonts; only file path + var name change.
- consumers: remove tmux_install_iconic_font: true from configure-linux-roles.yml; the desktop profile includes the new role instead of setting a flag.
- The boolean tmux_install_iconic_font is removed entirely: desktop includes the role, basic omits it (selection by profile/group, not a flag).

SEQUENCING: do this before the Phase 5a desktop role-import step so the verbatim import is conflict-free.
acceptance_criteria: tmux role has no font tasks/vars/scenario and its molecule default passes; new font role molecule default passes (font present + fc-cache rebuilt); version-update query+perform still track the nerd font (no version escapes tracking); no headless host installs the font while the desktop path still gets it; the eventual desktop role import carries no tmux_install_iconic_font override.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #37 (mtps-extract-nerd-font-role): nerd_font role extracted, tmux stripped, version-update wiring + docs/specs re-pointed, both molecule scenarios green and idempotent.

title: Synchronize Molecule test runs across concurrent agents with a lock file
description:
## Context
Confirmed twice during ansible-all-my-things-jqmx (tmux console-only fix):
a concurrent agent session running 'molecule test' for a different role
(claude_code) executed 'podman rm -f instance' and rebuilt its own container
also named 'instance' while another session's molecule scenario was using
that same container name. Every role's molecule/*/molecule.yml in this repo
hardcodes platforms: - name: instance, so the podman container namespace is
effectively a single shared global resource across all concurrent sessions
on one host, even when sessions are isolated via separate git worktrees.

This is a generalization of ansible-all-my-things-luon (already tracked,
non-blocking finding) into a concrete, prioritized fix.

## Proposed approach (from user)
Use a lock file to serialize Molecule runs across concurrent agents:
- The first agent to run tests creates a lock file.
- If lock-file creation fails (file already exists), another agent is
  currently running tests; the new agent must wait (poll/retry) rather than
  proceed.
- Tests may only run once the lock file is successfully created.
- After tests finish (success or failure), the lock file must be removed.
- Likely implementation: a small wrapper script (using `mkdir`-based or
  `flock`-based locking for atomicity), either as its own script or embedded
  into scripts/test-molecule-all.sh, and adopted by any other entry point
  that invokes `molecule test` directly (e.g. per-role manual runs, CI).

## Why P1
Confirmed twice to actively corrupt test runs (container killed mid-converge,
false failures) when two agents/sessions work in parallel on this repo at
the same time. This is the project's stated parallel-worktree workflow
(see AGENTS.md branch-naming and worktree guidance), so the collision is
expected to recur, not a rare edge case.
acceptance_criteria:
- A locking mechanism exists (script and/or wrapper) that prevents two
  concurrent `molecule test` invocations on this host from running at the
  same time, using a lock file created atomically (e.g. mkdir or flock) with
  wait/retry semantics for the second caller.
- The lock file is reliably removed after the test run completes, including
  on failure/interruption (trap-based cleanup or equivalent).
- scripts/test-molecule-all.sh (and any documented direct `molecule test`
  workflow in CONTRIBUTING.md or the molecule-testing skill) uses or
  documents the locking mechanism.
- Verified by manually running two molecule invocations concurrently and
  observing the second one wait rather than collide.
close_reason: Implemented mkdir-based lock wrapper (scripts/with-molecule-lock.sh), wired into test-molecule-all.sh and molecule-testing skill doc. Verified via 7-role full regression (0 regressions) and real two-role concurrency test (second waits, no collision).

title: setup-nodejs.yml: shell tasks lack changed_when, always report changed
description: playbooks/setup-nodejs.yml tasks 'Install LTS/Jod Node.js' (line 18) and 'Identify current Node.js version' (line 29) are shell: tasks with no changed_when, so they report changed=true on every run regardless of actual state (nvm install/use/alias and nvm current are effectively no-ops when the LTS version is already installed/active). Found during configure-basic-profile (010) Phase 4 acceptance test, US2 Scenario 1 (FR-020/SC-006) on a fresh tart VM (risa) - second run reported changed=3 instead of changed=0, 1 of which is 'Install LTS/Jod Node.js' and 1 is 'Identify current Node.js version'. Fix: add changed_when: false to 'Identify current Node.js version' (purely read-only). For 'Install LTS/Jod Node.js', register the result and set changed_when based on stdout/stderr indicating an actual install/alias change occurred (e.g. absence of 'is already installed' combined with an alias change), or restructure into separate idempotent steps. Pre-existing bug in setup-nodejs.yml, not introduced by 010 but blocks its SC-006.
close_reason: Fixed and merged: PR #24 (09j6), PR #26 (85t5), PR #25 (syit)

title: setup-users.yml: password_hash random salt breaks idempotency for user accounts
description: playbooks/setup-users.yml line 28, task 'Setup accounts ...': password: "{{ item.password | password_hash('sha512') }}" has no fixed salt. Ansible's password_hash filter generates a random salt each invocation when none given, so the hash differs every run -> the 'user' module always sees a 'changed' password and reports changed=true for every account (gandalf, galadriel) on every run, even with no actual change. Found during configure-basic-profile (010) Phase 4 acceptance test, US2 Scenario 1 (FR-020/SC-006) on a fresh tart VM (risa) - second run reported changed=3 instead of changed=0, 2 of which are this task's loop items. Fix: seed the salt deterministically, e.g. password_hash('sha512', 65534 | random(seed=item.name) | string), so the hash is stable across runs per user while still varying across users. Pre-existing bug in setup-users.yml, not introduced by 010 but blocks its SC-006.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/eudicy/ansible-all-my-things/pull/24
close_reason: Fixed and merged: PR #24 (09j6), PR #26 (85t5), PR #25 (syit)

title: setup-users.yml: PasswordAuthentication no overridden by cloud-init sshd_config.d drop-in
description: playbooks/setup-users.yml sets 'PasswordAuthentication no' via lineinfile on /etc/ssh/sshd_config. Ubuntu cloud images Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf near the top of sshd_config; 50-cloud-init.conf sets 'PasswordAuthentication yes' and is processed first (sshd is first-match-wins), so it wins over 60-cloudimg-settings.conf's 'no' and over our appended line. Effective sshd -T reports passwordauthentication yes despite the playbook's intent. Found during configure-basic-profile (010) Phase 4 acceptance test, Scenario 2 (FR-006/SC-002) on a fresh tart VM (risa). Fix: replace the lineinfile with a copy/template task writing /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-disable-password-auth.conf containing 'PasswordAuthentication no' (sorts before 50-cloud-init.conf, wins via first-match), keep the existing 'Restart SSH' handler notify. Pre-existing bug in setup-users.yml, not introduced by 010 but blocks its SC-002.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/eudicy/ansible-all-my-things/pull/26
close_reason: Fixed and merged: PR #24 (09j6), PR #26 (85t5), PR #25 (syit)

title: Create beads molecule pr-review-cycle for PR review workflow
description:
## Why

AI-implemented features end with a PR to origin/main. A human reviews that PR and files review findings. All findings must be resolved before the PR can merge. Without a standard template, each agent session re-invents this workflow ad-hoc.

## What

Create a proto (template epic with label 'template') named 'pr-review-cycle'. Structure:

- Proto epic: `pr-review-cycle` (label: template)
  - Story: 'Review PR and collect findings' (child of proto)
    - Task: 'Merge feature branch to origin/main' (child of story)
    - [Finding tasks added dynamically, each blocking the merge task]

When an agent instantiates the molecule for a feature:
1. Pour the proto: `bd mol pour pr-review-cycle`
2. Attach the user story as child of the parent feature: `bd update <story-id> --parent <feature-id>`
3. For each human review finding: create a task child of the story, wire as dep blocking the merge task

## Acceptance criteria

- `bd formula list` or `bd mol show pr-review-cycle` shows the proto
- Proto contains story 'Review PR and collect findings'
- Story contains task 'Merge feature branch to origin/main'
- `bd mol pour pr-review-cycle` instantiates the full structure correctly
- AGENTS.md documents when and how to instantiate this molecule
- `bd mol pour pr-review-cycle` is successfully run on this very issue (y7sa): story attached as child of y7sa, merge task present and wired correctly — the molecule validates itself
close_reason: Closed

title: dolt-sql-server fails to start: missing HOME directory for dolt user
description: Service fails with 'Failed to load the HOME directory: stat /home/dolt: no such file or directory'. Dolt reads $HOME at startup. Service user created with create_home: false, so no /home/dolt exists. Fix: set Environment=HOME={{ dolt_data_dir }} and WorkingDirectory={{ dolt_data_dir }} in the systemd service unit template.
close_reason: Fixed: added Environment=HOME and WorkingDirectory to service unit template. Molecule tests pass.

description:

title: Run Dolt SQL server locally so parallel agents can write to beads concurrently
description:
## Context

Agent VMs are ephemeral — destroyed after each session, recreated from scratch for the next. Beads data persists via git (`refs/dolt/data`), synchronized with `bd dolt push` at session end and restored with `bd bootstrap` (or `bd dolt pull`) at session start.

By default beads uses an embedded Dolt backend that permits only one concurrent writer. When multiple AI agents run in parallel via `my-omc-parallel-work`, all but one agent lose write access, causing lost task tracking and agent focus drift.

## Problem

Fresh VMs have no Dolt SQL server. Without one, parallel agents cannot write to beads concurrently.

## Goal

Create an Ansible role that installs Dolt and starts a Dolt SQL server as a systemd service on each new VM. All parallel agent sessions connect to this server instead of using embedded Dolt, eliminating write-lock contention.

## Scope

1. New Ansible role `roles/dolt_sql_server` with a Molecule test scenario
2. Install the Dolt binary (https://github.com/dolthub/dolt)
3. Configure and enable `dolt sql-server` as a systemd service (starts on every VM boot)
4. Update `.beads/config.yaml` to connect to the local Dolt SQL server
5. Add the role to `configure-linux-roles.yml` so it runs as part of base VM provisioning

## Role boundary

The role is responsible for: install + systemd service only.

Out of scope for the role:
- Database initialization (`dolt init`) — owned by `bd bootstrap`
- Data restore — owned by `bd dolt pull` / `bd bootstrap` at session start
- Data backup — owned by `bd dolt push` at session end

## Expected session lifecycle (after this feature)

1. VM created → provisioning runs `configure-linux-roles.yml` → Dolt SQL server starts
2. Agent session starts → `bd bootstrap` (or `bd dolt pull`) restores beads data from `refs/dolt/data`
3. Agents work, including parallel agents — all write to the shared local SQL server
4. Session ends → `bd dolt push` syncs beads data back to git

## Behavior

- Dolt SQL server starts automatically on each new VM boot via systemd
- All parallel agent sessions connect to the same local server
- Concurrent writes succeed without locking errors
- `.beads/config.yaml` points to the local Dolt SQL server

## Out of scope

- Database initialization (`dolt init`) — `bd bootstrap` owns this
- Data migration from existing embedded Dolt instances
- Remote/shared Dolt server (local to the agent VM only)
- Dolt Cloud or Dolt Hub integration
notes: eudicy/main merged (PR #15). Upstream PR #54 opened: https://github.com/wonderbird/ansible-all-my-things/pull/54 — awaiting wonderbird merge. After upstream merge: run migration (bd backup sync + bd backup restore --force), then close this issue.
close_reason: dolt_sql_server role implemented and merged to eudicy/main. Upstream PR #54 open at wonderbird/ansible-all-my-things.

title: Fix Pinning Lint CI failure on eudicy/main
description:
## Why

Pinning Lint job fails on eudicy/main after merge of fork-safe-docker-ci (commit 07e3ed5).

Run: https://github.com/eudicy/ansible-all-my-things/actions/runs/26385355353

## Two distinct failures

### 1. SARIF upload — CodeQL permission error
`upload-sarif` step fails with:
`Resource not accessible by integration`

zizmor itself exits with code 0 (scan passes). The SARIF upload to CodeQL fails because eudicy fork does not have GitHub Advanced Security / `security-events: write` permission on the GITHUB_TOKEN.

Fix: guard `upload-sarif` step with `if: github.repository == 'wonderbird/ansible-all-my-things'` (or equivalent repo owner check) so SARIF upload only runs on the canonical upstream repo.

### 2. New zizmor audit: `dependabot-cooldown`
zizmor 1.25.2 reports:
`insufficient cooldown in Dependabot updates: missing cooldown configuration`
Severity: Medium | Confidence: High | Rule: `zizmor/dependabot-cooldown`
Docs: https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#dependabot-cooldown

Fix: either add cooldown config to `.github/dependabot.yml` or suppress with rationale in `.github/zizmor.yml`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Pinning Lint job passes on eudicy/main
- SARIF upload does not cause job failure on fork
- dependabot-cooldown finding resolved or suppressed with documented rationale
notes:
Fixed in commit 8d9d608 on feature/fork-safe-docker-ci:
1. Replaced deprecated 'args:' input with config:/inputs:/advanced-security: native inputs
2. Added dependabot-cooldown: disable: true to .github/zizmor.yml with rationale
advanced-security: uses event_name != pull_request (capability-based condition)
Waiting for CI on wonderbird PR #48 to confirm green.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 41aaeb1 on eudicy/main. All PR #48 checks pass.

title: Add zizmorcore/zizmor-action to GitHub allow-list and ADR-002
description:
## Why

ADR-002 requires that adding a new action includes both pinning it AND adding it to the GitHub repository allow-list. zizmorcore/zizmor-action was added to pinning-lint.yml (SHA-pinned correctly as Tier A) but was not added to the allow-list in repository settings or to the allow-list section in ADR-002.

## What needs to be done

1. Add zizmorcore/zizmor-action@* to repository Settings → Actions → General → Allow select actions and reusable workflows
2. Add zizmorcore/zizmor-action@* to the Current entries list in the ADR-002 allow-list section (docs/architecture/decisions/002-github-actions-pinning-policy.md)

## Acceptance criteria

- zizmorcore/zizmor-action@* present in GitHub repository allow-list settings
- ADR-002 Current entries list includes zizmorcore/zizmor-action@*
- Both changes consistent with each other
close_reason: zizmorcore/zizmor-action@* already present in allow-list and ADR-002 current entries list.

title: Fix allow-list entries in ADR-002: add trailing commas
description: ADR-002 § Allow-List Configuration lists allow-list entries one per line without commas. This implies newlines work as separators in GitHub's Settings → Actions allow-list textbox, but they do not — GitHub requires comma-separated entries. Anyone copying the code block verbatim will get a broken allow-list. Fix: add trailing comma to each entry line in the code block.
close_reason: Fixed in this session

title: Add prescriptive per-action allow-list MUST to constitution Principle IX rule 4
description: Constitution Principle IX rule 4 currently says 'Each repository instance MUST enable the allow-list per ADR-002 § Allow-List Configuration' (fork setup) and 'See ADR-002 for full criteria' (soft cross-reference). An agent adding a new action may correctly apply the pinning tier rules and stop without following the soft reference to find the allow-list update step. Add a prescriptive sentence: 'When adding a new action to a workflow, agents MUST also add owner/repo@* to the repository allow-list per ADR-002 § Allow-List Configuration.' This closes the gap between a fork-setup MUST and a per-action-addition MUST.

title: Finding 4: Re-evaluate ADR-002 recommendation against mitigations + threat IDs
description:

  (a) the explicit threat IDs added in Finding 3, and
  (b) each option's mitigations

and test whether the Recommendation still stands as bare Option A.

Specific cases worth re-evaluating:
- Option B + auto-merge for actions/* SHA bumps + pinact tooling: D3 (patch velocity) gap closes substantially. Residual delta = trust in auto-merge. If acceptable, B becomes competitive (simpler rule, uniform SHA, no Tier B identity-trust dependency).
- Option C + Option F (Harden-Runner): runtime egress monitoring catches what tag-retargeting opens up. Worse on auditability (D2). Possibly acceptable for this repo's blast radius.
- Option A + Option G (allow-list): ADR already names this combo but does not commit to it as the recommendation. If recommended, recommendation should be 'A+G', not bare A.

Method: after Findings 1, 2, 3 land, do the option-vs-threat-vs-mitigation matrix walk. Update Recommendation accordingly. If no shift, document why explicitly.

Meta-fix: the Mitigations sections should be positioned in the ADR such that the reader cannot read pros/cons without already knowing the mitigations. (Note: skill-level fix tracked separately as Finding 6.)

title: Finding 3: Add explicit threat model section to ADR-002
description:
ADR-002 currently jumps from mixed-pinning observation to mechanism (Tier A/B) without enumerating the threats the policy is supposed to address. A decision-maker has to reverse-engineer the threat model from the pros/cons.

Fix: insert an explicit Threat Model section between Context and Decision Drivers. Enumerate threats and, for each, note in scope vs out of scope and whether the recommended option addresses it.

Candidate threats to discuss:
1. Pipeline credential leak — GHCR push token + OIDC ID token exposed to malicious action code running in the push job. (Highest blast radius.)
2. Malicious artefact published — image carrying backdoor under our signed identity; cosign signature still valid because we sign whatever we built. Downstream trust chain weaponized.
3. CI secret exfil — Ansible Vault password, SSH keys, cloud creds leaked via secrets.* env exposure to action code. (Currently low-surface in this repo's CI but framing should not assume that.)
4. Supply chain to maintainer dev box — compromised action writes malicious content into .devcontainer/ that gets pulled to local laptops. Indirect attack path.
5. Phishing / social-engineered PRs — adversary opens PR adding 'uses: evil/foo@v1' betting on reviewer fatigue. Policy + lint reduces blast radius.
6. Bot-net abuse of forks — fork CI as crypto miner / proxy. Likely out of scope; name and dismiss.

After enumeration: map each Considered Option to which threats it materially reduces. Reader should be able to see at a glance why Option A is recommended for the threat profile of this repo.

Acceptance:
- New Threat Model section exists between Context and Decision Drivers
- Each threat states: in/out of scope, owning option, severity for this repo
- Pros/cons of each option cross-reference threat IDs
- Recommendation paragraph cites threat IDs explicitly

Note: this finding pairs with Finding 4 (re-evaluate mitigations against threats). Once threats are explicit, the right mitigations become testable. Keep this finding scoped to the threat-model section; Finding 4 handles the solution re-evaluation.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace curl|sudo mv of container-structure-test /latest/ binary in CI
description:
Code-review finding from ADR-002 reviews. docker-publish.yml test job (lines ~107-110) downloads container-structure-test from a floating /latest/ download URL and sudo-mv's it into /usr/local/bin/ on every run, with no checksum or signature verification. The test job is needs: of the push job which holds packages:write + id-token:write — so a compromised /latest/ binary executes inside the credential path of the publish pipeline.

This is independent of the pinning policy (ADR-002). It is a separate supply-chain finding that ADR-002 explicitly lists as out of scope (and references this issue).

Acceptance:
- container-structure-test installed via pinned release tag (not /latest/)
- Either: SHA256 checksum verified against an upstream-published value, OR cosign verify of the released artefact if upstream signs releases
- No floating-version downloads in any job that is a needs: ancestor of the push job
- Document chosen approach in a short note inside docker-publish.yml header

Out of scope: switching tool, replacing with a GitHub Action wrapper (separate eval).
close_reason: Closed

title: Add CI lint job to enforce GitHub Actions pinning policy
description:
Enforce the two-tier pinning policy defined in ADR 002 (follow-up from finding urf). Add a workflow that fails the build when Tier A actions (third-party: docker/*, sigstore/*, anything with packages:write / id-token:write / signing / registry push) are pinned by tag instead of 40-char SHA. Tier B (first-party actions/* utilities) may keep floating major tags.

Tool evaluation REQUIRED before selection — assess upstream activity and health for each candidate via GitHub MCP or gh CLI (last release, commit cadence, open-issue trend, maintainer count, archived flag, CVE history):

- zizmor (Rust, built-in unpinned-uses audit)
- pinact (auto-pins + --check mode)
- ratchet (Go, ratchet check)

Record findings + chosen tool + rejection rationale in design field. Fallback: hand-rolled regex grep if all candidates fail health check.

Acceptance:
- Tool selected with documented health-check evidence
- Lint runs in CI on push + PR
- Tier A tag-pin in any workflow fails the job
- Tier B tag-pin passes
- Allow-list mechanism for documented exceptions (comment-based or config)
- README / ADR 002 cross-link to the lint job

Out of scope: rewriting existing pins (already conformant), changing the policy itself.
design: Tool health check (2026-05-21): zizmor (woodruffw/zizmor) v1.25.2 — 5182 stars, pushed 2026-05-20, not archived, most active project; pinact (suzuki-shunsuke/pinact) v3.10.1 — 1020 stars, pushed 2026-05-21, not archived, active but lacks native Tier A/B policy layer; ratchet (sethvargo/ratchet) v0.11.4 — 935 stars, last release 2025-06-27 (~11 months), slower cadence. Selected: zizmor. Rejection rationale — pinact: check mode flags all non-SHA pins uniformly, no built-in ref-pin policy for actions/* Tier B; ratchet: 11-month release gap indicates slower maintenance. zizmor provides native unpinned-uses.config.policies supporting hash-pin vs ref-pin per pattern, directly encoding the two-tier policy without wrappers. Config: .github/zizmor.yml. Workflow: .github/workflows/pinning-lint.yml. Verified: conformant workflows exit 0; docker/login-action@v3 (Tier A tag-pin) exits 14 with high-severity unpinned-uses error; actions/checkout@v6 (Tier B) exits 0.

title: Finding 2: Establish GitHub Actions pinning policy (SHA vs version tags)
description: Audit current pinning strategy in .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml. Currently mixed: SHA pins on docker/*, sigstore/* (artifact/credential actions) vs version tags on checkout, upload/download-artifact (utility actions). Create explicit policy document specifying which action categories warrant SHA pinning vs which can use version tags with Dependabot auto-patching. Rationale: SHAs prevent tag retagging attacks (immutable), version tags enable faster security patch velocity via Dependabot. Trade-off: readability vs maintainability vs attack surface. Aligns with Principle IX (CI/CD Pipeline Security) — explicit, auditable artifact provenance chain.

title: Refine docker-publish.yml: build → test → push order
description:
## Why

After ngu implements fork-safe artifact passing, the non-PR path (push to main/tags) still pushes to GHCR before running tests. This means a broken image can land in the registry.

## What needs to be done

Reorganize docker-publish.yml so the pipeline enforces build → test → push on ALL paths:

1. Build job: build image and export as tarball artifact (already done for PR path via ngu)
2. Test job: download artifact, load image, run container-structure-test — same job for both PR and non-PR paths
3. Push job: only runs after test job succeeds AND event is not a pull_request; pulls tarball artifact, loads image, pushes to GHCR, signs with cosign

This ensures GHCR only ever receives images that have passed structure tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- On PR: build → test → no push (same as ngu outcome)
- On push to main/tag: build → test → push (push only if test passes)
- No image ever reaches GHCR without a passing test job
- Cosign signing still runs after push
close_reason: build→test→push enforced on all paths. PR #6 merged to eudicy/ansible-all-my-things main. Run 25940172292 confirms: build×2, test×2, push×2 all pass. latest+latest-amd64 pushed and cosign-signed (sha256:578f41ef...). latest-arm64 pushed by arm64 leg.

title: Reduce Docker image size with multi-stage build
description:
## Why

Current .devcontainer/Dockerfile uses a single stage — build tools (pip,
pipx, git, python3-venv, gcc etc.) end up in the runtime image, inflating
size unnecessarily. Large images slow CI pull times and increase storage cost.

## Solution

Adopt multi-stage build pattern from BadWinniePooh/ansible-collection
(.docker/Dockerfile, sha b51cf5f):

- **builder stage**: full toolchain — python3, pip, pipx, git, openssh-client.
  Installs ansible-core via pipx, runs pip install -r requirements.txt,
  runs ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml.
- **runtime stage**: only python3 + openssh-client apt packages.
  Copy /root/.local (pipx venv + wrappers) and /root/.ansible (collections)
  from builder. No compilers, no pip, no pipx binary, no git in final image.

## Acceptance criteria

- .devcontainer/Dockerfile uses FROM ... AS builder + second FROM for runtime
- Final image contains ansible-playbook, ansible-galaxy executables
- Final image does NOT contain pip, pipx, git binaries
- container-structure-test suite passes on the new image
- Image size reduced vs. current single-stage build (document before/after in commit)
notes:
ubuntu:26.04 adopted for both stages. Key findings:
1. gpg-agent must be explicitly installed in ubuntu builder (not auto-dep of gpg unlike Debian)
2. AWS CLI PyInstaller binary uses $ORIGIN RPATH — when COPY breaks the symlink chain (from /usr/local/bin/aws into dist/), the bootloader looks for libpython3.14.so.1.0 in /usr/local/bin/ and fails. Fix: symlink /usr/local/bin/aws -> /usr/local/aws-cli/v2/current/bin/aws so bootloader resolves the real path inside dist/ where the bundled library lives.
3. locales-all dropped (was 300MB uncompressed); ubuntu base has locales package sufficient for ansible.
4. Final image: 686 MB. Tests: 6/6 pass.
5. container-structure-test needs Podman socket active: systemctl --user start podman.socket
close_reason: ubuntu:26.04 base adopted; all 6 container-structure-tests pass; image 686 MB

title: Fork-safe Docker CI: fix docker-publish.yml for fork compatibility
description:
## Why

docker-publish.yml hardcodes 'wonderbird/ansible-toolchain' as image name. On forks:
- Push steps fail (read-only GITHUB_TOKEN)
- Test jobs validate wrong image (upstream :latest, not the built one)
- Both architectures untested on PRs

Breaks CI for all contributors working on forks.

## What needs to be done

Implement the design from docs/features/fork-safe-docker-ci/:

1. Replace hardcoded image name with `${{ github.repository_owner }}/ansible-toolchain`
2. Split build into per-arch matrix: ubuntu-24.04 (amd64) + ubuntu-24.04-arm (arm64)
3. PR path: build → docker save tarball → upload artifact → test job downloads + loads
4. Non-PR path: push to ghcr.io → test job pulls from registry
5. Scope GHA cache keys per arch
6. Guard cosign/push steps with `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`

## Acceptance criteria

- PR from any fork: both archs build and test with no registry push
- Push to main: images published to fork owner's ghcr.io namespace
- No hardcoded 'wonderbird' in workflow file
notes: Feature branch: feature/fork-safe-docker-ci

title: Add the install-only AI agent profile
description:
Deliver the actual capability: a profile that installs AI tooling with zero global per-user agent config, for a user who configures agents per project themselves.

What:
- Add the install-only profile as a flavor in the nested topology (base roles minus claude_code_config).
- Roles: full basic dev stack (podman, ruby, vim, python, nodejs, tmux, dolt_sql_server, github_cli, beads_*) + install-only AI CLIs: claude_code (binary only), opencode, specify_cli, rtk.
- ai_agent_workspace included as clone-only: the skill library is cloned into the user's home but NOT symlinked into ~/.claude/skills (symlinking lives in claude_code_config, which this profile omits).
- No Cursor. No ~/.claude settings, OMC, plugins, MCP, rtk init -g, or bashrc agent config.

Depends on the claude_code split (needs install-only claude_code). Sequenced after the topology refactor.
acceptance_criteria: New-profile host has claude, opencode, specify, rtk binaries working. ~/.claude has no global config (no settings.json opinionation, no plugins, no MCP, no skills symlinks); .bashrc has no agent block. ai-agent-workspace repo present under the user's home, unsymlinked. Existing basic/desktop profiles unaffected. Local VM validation passes.

title: Refactor profile topology to base plus desktop-extension nesting (DRY)
description:
configure-profile-roles.yml carries two flat plays with copy-pasted role lists (an explicitly accepted Principle XI exception). This duplication makes any shared-role change a two-place edit and blocks clean reuse of the AI tooling across headless and desktop.

What:
- Introduce a shared base group whose children are the profile groups, so a desktop host inherits base membership ([<base>:children] with the profile groups).
- Collapse the duplicated lists into a base play (hosts: <base>, all shared roles) plus a desktop-extension play (hosts: desktop, GUI-only roles: nerd_font, google_chrome, obsidian, etc.).
- Confirm existing when: 'desktop' in group_names gating in configure-profile.yml still resolves (group_names contains both base and desktop). Windows group untouched.
- Move shared vars to base-level group_vars; keep desktop-only vars at desktop level (child overrides parent).
- Remove the accepted-duplication comment.

Behavior-preserving refactor: same roles reach same hosts, declared once. No new capability. Sequence before the install-only profile feature by intent.
acceptance_criteria: Resolved role set per basic host and per desktop host is identical to pre-refactor (prove via --list-tasks/dry compare or local VM converge). No role executes twice on any host. Desktop setup gating still fires correctly; headless hosts get no GUI roles. Local VM validation passes per testing.md (playbook-level, not Molecule).

title: Split claude_code into install-only role plus claude_code_config role
description:
Binary install and global per-user configuration are separate responsibilities glued into one role, which prevents installing Claude Code without applying global config. Splitting them is the prerequisite for any install-only profile and improves single-responsibility.

What:
- claude_code keeps binary install + OS deps only (install-deps.yml, install-claude-code.yml).
- New role claude_code_config receives ALL global config: settings.json merge (env, hooks, teammateMode), OMC CLI + plugins (oh-my-claudecode, caveman, context7), exa MCP config, ~/.claude/skills symlinking of the ai-agent-workspace skills, rtk init -g, .bashrc CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, OMC setup-prompt copy.
- Existing basic and desktop plays list BOTH roles so their end state is identical to today.
- claude_code_config declares claude_code in meta/main.yml dependencies (hard runtime consumer) and keeps explicit play ordering.
- claude_code_config gets its own Molecule scenario (create->converge->idempotence->verify->destroy).
acceptance_criteria: A host in basic/desktop ends equivalent to pre-split (settings.json, plugins, symlinks, bashrc all present). A host with only claude_code applied has the binary and NO ~/.claude opinionation. Both roles pass molecule test and an idempotence re-run reports zero changes. Version pin stays in claude_code defaults; version-update wiring unchanged.

title: Install-only AI agent profile via layered profile topology
description:
A single-user VM should be provisionable for running many kinds of agents (general personal-assistance agents; per-project coding agents such as Claude Code + oh-my-claudecode for one project, OpenCode + oh-my-openagent for another) WITHOUT the provisioning step imposing any global per-user agent configuration. The user clones each project and configures its agent themselves when starting work.

Today the claude_code role bundles binary install with heavy global config (~/.claude/settings.json, OMC/plugins, MCP, skills symlinks, rtk init -g, .bashrc), so there is no way to get the tooling without the opinionation.

Deliver an install-only AI-tooling profile in three dependency-ordered, low-risk increments. The first two are behavior-preserving (no user-visible change); the new capability lands only in the third. Along the way, retire the accepted basic/desktop role-list duplication by making desktop an extension layer over a shared base group.

Scope boundary: provisions tooling only. No project cloning, no per-project agent setup, no global ~/.claude config in the new profile.

Children (in order): split claude_code -> topology refactor -> install-only profile.

Constitution touchpoints: II (role-first, Molecule per role, meta dependency), XI (DRY nesting), IV (YAGNI per increment), III (local test before cloud).

title: Human review: verify fixes for ansible-all-my-things-9hzb findings; invoke /record-findings ansible-all-my-things-9hzb
description:
IMPORTANT: This task MUST be executed by the human reviewer, not an AI agent, and MUST NOT be closed by an AI agent.

Review procedure -- derive everything live; trust no pre-baked list or order:

1. List the gate's children (open and closed) via 'bd show ansible-all-my-things-9hzb', then exclude any already labeled human-reviewed and this review task itself. What remains is the unreviewed set.

2. For each finding in the unreviewed set, locate its fixing commit(s) with 'git log --no-pager --grep=<finding-id>' (the commit skill mandates a Refs: <finding-id> trailer, so every fix is discoverable). A finding with no commit is not yet fixed -- leave it unlabeled for a later round; do not review it now.

3. From the files actually changed across those commits, group findings by file/area and order them dependency-first -- computed in hindsight from the real diffs, so the reviewer opens each file once. For a large or tangled finding set, delegate this ordering to a high-reasoning, read-only subagent. Skip delegation for a small set.

4. Walk through each finding in that order, confirming each fix. The moment the human accepts or rejects a fix, mark that finding reviewed: 'bd update <finding-id> --add-label human-reviewed'. For a rejected fix, also file a new child finding under the gate -- it stays unlabeled and is reviewed in the next round.
close_reason: fixed and verified

title: fetch-claude-code-version.yml lacks fail-loud guard on manifest platform keys
description:
playbooks/update-versions/tasks/fetch-claude-code-version.yml's 'Extract Claude Code checksums from release manifest' task accesses _claude_code_manifest.json.platforms['linux-x64'].checksum and ['linux-arm64'].checksum directly, with no assert/fail guard beforehand. If Anthropic ever restructures manifest.json or renames a platform key, this fails with Jinja's generic missing-key error rather than a clear, actionable message -- violates Constitution Principle XII (Fail Loud: 'Failure messages MUST identify the source (variable name, URL, file path) to enable diagnosis without guesswork').

Established precedent in the same directory: fetch-flutter-version.yml has an explicit 'Fail if latest stable Flutter entry is missing required fields' assert; fetch-nodejs-version.yml has 'Assert a Node.js LTS version was resolved'; fetch-github-release.yml has three explicit fail-loud checks (rate limit, unexpected status, missing tag_name).

Fix: add an ansible.builtin.assert before the set_fact, checking both 'linux-x64' and 'linux-arm64' keys exist in _claude_code_manifest.json.platforms, with a fail_msg naming the manifest URL and the missing key(s).
close_reason: Human-reviewed and accepted (gate ansible-all-my-things-9hzb)

title: molecule idempotence phase failed with podman UNREACHABLE (transient?) on roles/nodejs

Suspected cause: this molecule run happened concurrently with roles/specify_cli's molecule test (both podman-driver, launched in parallel background tasks), possible podman resource contention. close_reason: Confirmed transient: retried roles/nodejs molecule test in isolation (no concurrent podman jobs) and it passed the full lifecycle cleanly (destroy/syntax/create/prepare/converge/idempotence/verify/destroy, real exit code 0). Root cause: running nodejs and specify_cli molecule tests concurrently caused podman resource contention, manifesting as an UNREACHABLE 'Failed to create temporary directory' error at the idempotence phase's Gathering Facts task. Not a defect in the nodejs version-pinning changes. Lesson: avoid running multiple podman-driver molecule tests concurrently in this environment.

title: Rewrite checksum-verification-pattern.md + version-update-playbooks.md: static pin is the rule, retire dynamic-resolve-frozen-install framing
description:
Per decision ansible-all-my-things-jvs4.1.14: explicit version (+ checksum, where applicable) MUST be stated statically in each role's defaults/main.yml, refreshed only by playbooks/update-versions/perform-updates.yml -- flutter is the reference example. Dynamic-resolve-at-converge-time (live 'get latest release' + live checksum fetch, frozen only by a stat-gate) is retired as the recommended pattern.

docs/architecture/concepts/checksum-verification-pattern.md needs:
- 'Idempotency semantics' section rewritten: remove the framing that dynamic-resolve+stat-gate is the deliberate, preferred model for rtk/beads/nodejs. State the static-pin model (version+checksum both explicit in defaults/main.yml, matching flutter/obsidian/dolt_sql_server/opencode) as the rule instead. A stat-gate on the resulting binary path may still be used for skip-if-present idempotency, but the SOURCE of truth for what to install must be the pinned default var, not a live upstream query at converge time.
- 'Reference implementations' section rewritten: stop citing rtk/beads/nodejs's CURRENT (live-resolve) code as reference implementations of the recommended pattern -- once ansible-all-my-things-m0av.1/.2/.3 land, point to their POST-migration static-pin state instead, alongside flutter/obsidian as the original examples.
- Add explicit cross-reference to docs/architecture/version-update-playbooks.md (this doc explains HOW to verify a checksum for an already-pinned version + why the pin must be static; that doc explains the centralized query/refresh mechanism that keeps the pin current).

docs/architecture/version-update-playbooks.md needs:
- Add explicit cross-reference back to checksum-verification-pattern.md.
- Tool table gets new rows for rtk, beads (bd), beads (bv), nodejs, specify_cli, and Claude Code once each respective migration bead (m0av.1-4, jvs4.1.14.1) lands -- do not add rows before each tool's own migration bead actually lands, so the doc never describes an aspirational state as current.

GATE: markdownlint clean on both files. No molecule surface (docs-only) unless a role's own migration bead already requires molecule re-run for unrelated reasons.
close_reason: Verified docs/architecture/concepts/checksum-verification-pattern.md and docs/architecture/version-update-playbooks.md already carried the full rewrite: Idempotency semantics section states static-pin as the rule (not dynamic-resolve+stat-gate); Reference implementations section points to POST-migration rtk/beads/nodejs/claude_code code alongside flutter/obsidian; version-update-playbooks.md tool table has rows for rtk, beads(bd), beads(bv), nodejs, specify_cli, claude_code (confirmed each migration bead m0av.1-4 + jvs4.1.14.1 closed, so gate against adding rows early was satisfied); bidirectional cross-references present both files; markdownlint clean both files; spot-checked roles/rtk/tasks+defaults against doc's claim (static rtk_version pin, no live resolve) - matches. Found and fixed one gap during verification: version-update-playbooks.md still said 'nine tools'/'nine tracked tools' in 3 spots (stale from before this rewrite, table now has 14 distinct roles) and 'current 14-tool scale' in a 4th spot - all reworded to avoid hardcoding a count that goes stale as tools are added/removed.

title: Pin Claude Code version + checksum in defaults/main.yml, switch to verify-before-placement (supersedes gx4a)
description:
Supersedes ansible-all-my-things-gx4a: gx4a proposed the same direct-download+verify shift for claude_code's binary install, but under the OLD dynamic-resolve-frozen-at-first-install model ('same frozen-at-first-install stat-gate model already used by rtk/beads/nodejs') -- that model is rejected by decision ansible-all-my-things-jvs4.1.14 in favor of an explicit static pin (flutter-style). gx4a is closed as superseded by this bead; do not implement gx4a's approach separately.

Add claude_code_version + per-arch static checksum (e.g. claude_code_sha256_linux_x64 / claude_code_sha256_linux_arm64) to roles/claude_code/defaults/main.yml. Values come from Anthropic's per-version manifest.json (already fetched by the existing role at converge time; for the pin, extract both platforms' checksums ONCE at update-time instead).

Update roles/claude_code/tasks/install-claude-code.yml: replace the current always-refetch-latest + always-reverify-installed-binary-post-hoc sequence with: use the pinned claude_code_version to build the manifest-derived binary URL directly, verify via a literal 'sha256:{{ claude_code_sha256_... }}' checksum BEFORE placement (get_url native checksum param), and add a stat-gate consistent with the new model (skip entirely if the pinned version's binary is already present) -- this also lets claude_code drop its unique always-reverify-on-rerun behavior, converging its idempotency model with rtk/beads/nodejs's stat-gate shape (though the SOURCE of the gate is now the static pin, not a live 'latest' resolution).

Needs a NEW fetch task (playbooks/update-versions/tasks/fetch-claude-code-version.yml or similar) since the checksum source is a per-version manifest.json lookup, not a raw computed tarball hash or GitHub-Releases tag_name alone -- fetch both the release tag (via fetch-github-release.yml, github_repo: anthropics/claude-code) AND the manifest.json's two platform checksums, wire all three (version + 2 checksums) into query-versions.yml/perform-updates.yml.

Update docs/architecture/concepts/checksum-verification-pattern.md's 'Idempotency semantics' section once this lands -- it currently contrasts claude_code's always-reverify model against rtk/beads/nodejs; that contrast goes away. Coordinate with the sibling docs-policy bead under this same decision issue so the two edits don't conflict.

molecule test full lifecycle for roles/claude_code must stay green after the switch.

Supersedes closed ansible-all-my-things-gx4a (same direct-download+verify shift, but under the rejected dynamic-resolve model). Fail-loud gate manually verified (staled pin -> non-zero exit -> reverted). Molecule full lifecycle green (destroy/syntax/create/prepare/converge/idempotence/verify/destroy, all 31 verify assertions passed including the composed rtk+nodejs+ai_agent_workspace+claude_code scenario). docs/architecture/concepts/checksum-verification-pattern.md's 'Idempotency semantics' section update is reserved for the separately-tracked ansible-all-my-things-jvs4.1.14.2, not touched here. title: Decision: reconcile static-pin update-playbooks vs dynamic-resolve frozen-install versioning
description:
Two version-tracking mechanisms now coexist in this repo, with no stated precedence:

1. Static-pin + manual update playbooks (docs/architecture/version-update-playbooks.md): defaults/main.yml pins an exact version + checksum for 9 tools (flutter, gitmux, nerd_font, android_studio, java, dolt, opencode, github_cli, obsidian). query-versions.yml detects drift, perform-updates.yml applies it, maintainer reviews diff and commits manually.

2. Dynamic-resolve + frozen-at-first-install (docs/architecture/concepts/checksum-verification-pattern.md): roles/rtk, roles/beads (bd/bv), roles/nodejs resolve 'latest' from upstream (GitHub releases / nodejs.org index.json) at configure time, verify checksum inline, and gate re-runs on a version-agnostic stat path (e.g. /usr/local/bin/rtk) so re-converge never re-resolves. No version is ever written to defaults/main.yml.

Constitution Principle II's wiring requirement is textually scoped to roles that 'pin a tool version in defaults/main.yml' -- rtk/beads/nodejs deliberately do not, specifically to avoid that trigger (stated rationale in jvs4.1.13's close notes). This makes them textually exempt from mechanism 1.

ansible-all-my-things-m0av (open, parent jvs4) already proposes wiring rtk/beads/nodejs/specify_cli into 'the version-update mechanism' -- but doesn't resolve which mechanism, or whether mechanism 1 needs a new query-only mode (report currently-resolved version vs latest upstream, no defaults/main.yml write, since there is nothing to write to) rather than literally reusing perform-updates.yml's pin-and-checksum-replace approach.

Needs an explicit decision, recorded either as a constitution amendment (if the two-mechanism split is intentional and permanent) or as a rewrite of m0av's scope (if mechanism 1 should grow a query-only mode to cover mechanism 2's tools). Until decided, m0av should not be implemented on an unstated premise.
close_reason: Decided: explicit version (+ checksum, where applicable) MUST be stated statically in defaults/main.yml, refreshed only by playbooks/update-versions/perform-updates.yml -- flutter is the reference. Dynamic-resolve-frozen-at-first-install (rtk, beads bd/bv, nodejs's current shipped code) is retired as the recommended pattern; specify_cli's inline pin moves to defaults too; claude_code needs a full migration. Tracked via ansible-all-my-things-m0av.1 (rtk), m0av.2 (bd/bv), m0av.3 (nodejs), m0av.4 (specify_cli), jvs4.1.14.1 (claude_code, supersedes gx4a, closed), jvs4.1.14.2 (docs rewrite, durable record of this decision lands there). Not implemented inline -- filed as separate tracked work per Principle VIII.

title: Rework nodejs role: drop nvm, pin a specific Node.js version directly
description:
REJECTED-then-refiled: jvs4.1.6's nodejs role installed nvm (per-user Node version manager) to install one fixed version per desktop user. Rejected on review: nvm's value is switching between multiple installed Node versions over time on a long-lived machine -- this repo's VMs are created/destroyed per Constitution's disposable-VM model, so that flexibility is unused weight. Fix: install one specific Node.js version directly (no version manager), defaulting to latest LTS. Role KEEPS its current name roles/nodejs -- no rename.

DECIDED (this is now an execution contract, not an open design question):

1. Version resolution: resolve "latest LTS" DYNAMICALLY each run via nodejs.org's index.json (parse for the newest entry with a truthy lts field) -- do NOT pin a static version in defaults/main.yml (today's role already avoids this by pinning inline in tasks, not defaults, so this doesn't newly trigger Constitution Principle II's version-update-mechanism wiring; dynamic-resolve is consistent with existing rtk/beads precedent, not a new exception). MANDATORY fail-loud assert: after parsing index.json, assert the resolved version string is non-empty before constructing any download/checksum URL (Principle XII), mirroring roles/beads/tasks/main.yml's "Assert bv checksum was found in the manifest" pattern.

2. Install mechanism: direct-download+verify the release tarball against nodejs.org's per-release SHASUMS256.txt via get_url's native checksum: URL param -- same shape as roles/rtk/tasks/main.yml. System-wide install (not per-user).

3. Freeze-gate (MANDATORY, this is what keeps dynamic-resolve idempotent): stat the VERSION-AGNOSTIC path /usr/local/bin/node ONLY. On hit, skip the ENTIRE resolve+download+npm block -- zero network calls on re-converge. Do NOT key the gate on a resolved version number (that would re-resolve+compare every run = silent auto-upgrade on every new LTS release = Principle I violation, the exact bug this gate exists to prevent). Mirror roles/rtk/tasks/main.yml:3-11 exactly.

4. Global npm packages (eslint, markdownlint-cli, prettier, typescript): single system-wide "npm install --global" run, not a per-user loop. The creates: idempotency guard must key on the VERSION-AGNOSTIC path /usr/local/lib/node_modules/typescript, not any per-version nvm path (which becomes undefined once nvm is gone -- Principle XII fail if left as-is).

5. Retire the first_desktop_user-shared-npm-guard hack entirely (verified via grep: first_desktop_user is ONLY referenced inside roles/nodejs/ itself -- defaults/main.yml:8, tasks/main.yml:49,54,67, README.md:24, molecule/default/verify.yml:46 -- safe to remove, no cross-role reference).

6. roles/nodejs/molecule/default/verify.yml MUST be rewritten in the same commit: replace the nvm-based assertions (stat ~/.nvm/nvm.sh, nvm current, nvm-sourcing) with: stat /usr/local/bin/node (version-agnostic), direct "node --version"/"npm --version" (NO nvm sourcing), "npm list -g --depth=0" (NO nvm sourcing) asserting the 4 global packages present.

7. roles/nodejs/molecule/default/converge.yml: reduce from 2 test users to 1. The 2-user scenario existed solely to exercise the first_desktop_user-keyed shared creates: guard across users (a per-user divergence risk) -- system-wide install definitionally retires all per-user divergence in this role, so 1 user is the correct scope, not a coverage loss. State this rationale in a comment so a future maintainer doesn't cargo-cult 2 users back for the now-defunct reason.

8. roles/nodejs/meta/main.yml's description ("Install nvm and Node.js LTS plus common global npm packages") is stale and MUST be corrected -- no more nvm.

9. roles/nodejs/README.md MUST be corrected, not just appended to: remove the stale nvm-framing opening (currently describes "installs nvm and the Node.js LTS release... for each desktop user"), remove the first_desktop_user variable row, remove the whole "nvm version (v0.40.3) is pinned as an inline literal... to avoid triggering Principle II" paragraph (no longer applicable, nvm is gone). ADD instead: a paragraph stating dynamic-resolve-no-static-pin is a DELIBERATE, NAMED trade-off -- different VMs provisioned at different times may land on different Node LTS majors, favoring the disposable-VM model over cross-provision reproducibility. This is an accepted sacrifice, not an oversight.

10. CROSS-ROLE FIX, MANDATORY, SAME COMMIT AS ABOVE (do not split into a separate commit/push): roles/claude_code/tasks/install-omc-cli.yml (lines ~15 and ~26) currently does "source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && ..." unconditionally -- once nvm is removed by this finding, that breaks claude_code (its converge.yml already composes nodejs). Drop the nvm-sourcing prefix, use system PATH directly (verify /usr/local/bin is reachable on claude_code's become_user shells first -- add an explicit "environment: PATH" override if a live check shows it's needed). Collapse the per-user omc-install-check-and-install loop to a single system-wide run (verify oh-my-claude-sisyphus has no per-user state first -- expected to have none, analogous to bd/bv's own system-wide move in jvs4.1.9, but confirm). roles/claude_code/molecule/default/verify.yml (line ~197) -- drop the nvm-sourcing prefix from the "omc --version" check.

ALSO IN SCOPE, SAME COMMIT: two claude_code docs currently assert the nvm mechanism this finding removes and MUST be corrected, not left stale:
- roles/claude_code/README.md (around line 28): "The nodejs role applied first, providing ~/.nvm/nvm.sh and a Node.js LTS install for each target user" -- rewrite to describe the new system-wide node/npm install instead of ~/.nvm/nvm.sh.
- roles/claude_code/DESIGN.md (around lines 71-73): "The nvm/Node.js dependency this role's omc CLI install needs is provisioned by the nodejs role, declared as a hard meta/main.yml dependency (it unconditionally sources ~/.nvm/nvm.sh, per the decision test in docs/architecture/concepts/role-dependency-declaration.md)." -- the nodejs meta-dependency statement stays accurate; only the "sources ~/.nvm/nvm.sh" clause needs to change to describe the new system-wide node/npm mechanism.

11. GATE (do not commit/push until BOTH pass): roles/nodejs full molecule lifecycle AND roles/claude_code full molecule lifecycle, standalone runs, in that order. This is ONE atomic commit spanning both roles -- do NOT push after nodejs's molecule alone; that would leave claude_code's molecule red on the remote (its converge already composes nodejs). Run both, confirm both green, THEN one commit, THEN push.

12. Housekeeping after this lands: update bd issue ansible-all-my-things-m0av's description (currently says "nodejs (nvm)") to reflect nvm's removal -- dynamic-resolve doesn't pin a version to track the same way nvm's inline pin did.

Supersedes the current roles/nodejs/ role and its wiring, added in commit 8a95679 (+ follow-up 7fd8616).
close_reason: Fixed: nodejs role drops nvm, direct-download+verify Node LTS system-wide, matching cross-role claude_code fix, commit 9953614. m0av housekeeping done.

title: Human review: verify fixes for ansible-all-my-things-my7x findings; invoke /record-findings ansible-all-my-things-my7x
description:
IMPORTANT: This task MUST be executed by the human reviewer, not an AI agent, and MUST NOT be closed by an AI agent.

Review procedure -- derive everything live; trust no pre-baked list or order:

1. List the gate's children (open and closed) via 'bd show ansible-all-my-things-my7x', then exclude any already labeled 'human-reviewed' and this review task itself. What remains is the unreviewed set. This keeps review rounds from overlapping: findings accepted in an earlier round carry the label and drop out, while findings filed during that earlier round are still unlabeled and surface now -- so no finding is reviewed twice and none is missed.

2. For each finding in the unreviewed set, locate its fixing commit(s) with 'git log --no-pager --grep=<finding-id>' (the commit skill mandates a 'Refs: <finding-id>' trailer, so every fix is discoverable). A finding with no commit is not yet fixed -- leave it unlabeled for a later round; do not review it now.

3. From the files actually changed across those commits, group findings by file/area and order them dependency-first -- computed in hindsight from the real diffs, so the reviewer opens each file once. For a large or tangled finding set, delegate this ordering step to a high-reasoning, read-only subagent (e.g. an Opus-class model), which returns the grouped, ordered plan. Skip delegation for a small set.

4. Walk through each finding in that order, confirming each fix. The moment the human accepts or rejects a fix, mark that finding reviewed: 'bd update <finding-id> --add-label human-reviewed'. For a rejected fix, also file a new child finding under the gate -- it stays unlabeled and is reviewed in the next round.
close_reason: Reviewed my7x.1 (accepted-risk doc) and my7x.2 (debug removal), both accepted

title: Wire rtk/beads/nodejs/specify_cli into version-update mechanism
description: None of rtk, beads (bd/bv), nodejs, and specify_cli (spec-kit) are wired into playbooks/update-versions/ (query-versions.yml, perform-updates.yml, per-tool fetch task). This is a pre-existing gap. rtk/beads/nodejs are all stat-gated/frozen-at-first-install by design (see docs/architecture/concepts/checksum-verification-pattern.md) -- each resolves its "latest" version dynamically at first install and never re-resolves afterward, so refreshing any of them to a newer upstream release has no path other than this version-update-mechanism wiring, making this a load-bearing follow-up, not an aspiration. nodejs (roles/nodejs) previously used a pinned nvm version (v0.40.3); nvm was later removed entirely (jvs4.1.13) in favor of a direct, dynamically-resolved Node.js LTS install with no static pin anywhere -- same frozen-at-first-install shape as rtk/beads, not a special case. specify_cli's inline v0.8.18 pin remains the one static (non-dynamic) pin among these four, kept inline in tasks rather than defaults/main.yml specifically to avoid triggering Constitution Principle II's version-update-mechanism wiring. When version pinning/refresh is desired for any of these tools, wire it per Constitution Principle II (fetch task under playbooks/update-versions/tasks/, read-current-pin + upstream-query in query-versions.yml, update task + fetch include in perform-updates.yml).
notes: Decision (jvs4.1.14, 2026-07-08): static-pin + version-update-playbooks.md mechanism is the one to converge on for rtk/bd/bv/nodejs -- NOT the dynamic-resolve-frozen-at-first-install design jvs4.1.9 (beads) and jvs4.1.13 (nodejs) just shipped (rtk's earlier-accepted pattern is superseded too). Scope for this issue now includes: add a version+checksum pin to each role's defaults/main.yml, add a fetch task + query-versions.yml/perform-updates.yml wiring per Constitution Principle II, matching the 9 existing tools. docs/architecture/concepts/checksum-verification-pattern.md will need a follow-up rewrite once this lands -- it currently documents the dynamic-resolve design as the preferred pattern, which this decision supersedes.
close_reason: All 4 children closed: m0av.1 (rtk), m0av.2 (bd/bv), m0av.3 (nodejs), m0av.4 (specify_cli). Each pinned per Constitution Principle II and wired into playbooks/update-versions/{query,perform}-versions.yml. Commits b30109f, ba36f12, 8454132, 5d42906, ccf1d9c (shared wiring), plus doc fixes (b4ab319) and a post-implementation cleanup pass (a2feff8). Per jvs4.1.14's decision, static-pin (flutter-style) superseded the dynamic-resolve model this issue originally described; scope was updated accordingly per that decision's notes. Two of the issue's own descriptions were found stale during implementation and corrected via filed+resolved findings (m0av.3's nodejs_* vs node_* naming: ansible-all-my-things-teqg; m0av.4's incorrect 'no molecule scenario' claim: ansible-all-my-things-a6m8). title: Human review: verify fixes for ekvr findings; invoke /record-findings ekvr
description:
IMPORTANT: This task MUST be executed by the human reviewer, not an AI agent, and MUST NOT be closed by an AI agent.

Review procedure — derive everything live; trust no pre-baked list or order:

1. List the gate's children (open and closed) via `bd show ansible-all-my-things-ekvr`, then exclude any already labeled `human-reviewed` and this review task itself. What remains is the unreviewed set.

2. For each finding in the unreviewed set, locate its fixing commit(s) with `git log --no-pager --grep=<finding-id>` (the `commit` skill mandates a `Refs: <finding-id>` trailer). A finding with no commit is not yet fixed — leave it unlabeled for a later round.

3. From the files actually changed across those commits, group findings by file/area and order them dependency-first. For a large or tangled finding set, delegate this to a high-reasoning read-only subagent.

4. Walk through each finding in that order, confirming each fix. When the human accepts or rejects a fix, mark it reviewed: `bd update <finding-id> --add-label human-reviewed`. For a rejected fix, file a new child finding under the gate — it stays unlabeled and is reviewed in the next round.

title: java role: SDKMAN download of pinned 21.0.11-tem fails in CI
description:
Molecule converge fails for the java role in CI (run 28327185768, PR #88 to wonderbird/ansible-all-my-things).

TASK: 'java : Install Temurin JDK per user'
COMMAND: bash -c 'source /home/testuser/.sdkman/bin/sdkman-init.sh && sdk install java 21.0.11-tem'
ERROR: Download reaches 100% (curl progress bar completes) then SDKMAN reports 'Download has failed, aborting! Can not install java 21.0.11-tem at this time...' — rc=1.

Root cause: java_sdkman_identifier: "21.0.11-tem" is pinned in roles/java/defaults/main.yml. This version appears to have been removed or yanked from the SDKMAN/Adoptium Temurin distribution. The download completes but fails checksum or the catalog entry no longer resolves.

Fix: update java_sdkman_identifier to the currently available Temurin JDK 21 LTS version via SDKMAN, and update the version-update-playbooks wiring accordingly (Principle II).

title: Human review: verify fixes for yyoy.4 findings; invoke /record-findings yyoy.4
description:
IMPORTANT: This task MUST be executed by the human reviewer, not an AI agent, and MUST NOT be closed by an AI agent.

Review procedure — derive everything live; trust no pre-baked list or order:

1. List the gate's children (open AND closed) via:
     bd show ansible-all-my-things-yyoy.4
   Then exclude any already labeled 'human-reviewed' and this review task
   itself. What remains is the unreviewed set. This keeps review rounds from
   overlapping: findings accepted in an earlier round carry the label and drop
   out, while findings filed DURING that earlier round are still unlabeled and
   surface now — so nothing is reviewed twice and nothing is missed.

2. For each finding in the unreviewed set, locate its fixing commit(s) with:
     git log --no-pager --grep=<finding-id>
   (the commit skill mandates a 'Refs: <finding-id>' trailer). A finding with
   no commit is 'not yet fixed' — leave it unlabeled for a later round.

3. From the files actually changed across those commits, group findings by
   file/area and order them dependency-first — computed in hindsight from the
   real diffs, so each file is opened once. This is the one analytically hard
   step. For a large or tangled set, delegate it to a high-reasoning, read-only
   subagent (e.g. an Opus-class model), which returns the grouped, ordered
   plan; skip the delegation for a small set. Step 4 stays in the main thread
   regardless — it is a turn-by-turn dialogue and cannot be delegated.

4. Walk through each finding in that order (invoke /record-findings yyoy.4).
   The moment you accept OR reject a fix, mark it reviewed:
     bd update <finding-id> --add-label human-reviewed
   For a rejected fix, also file a new child finding under the gate — it stays
   unlabeled and is reviewed in the next round.

Why no finding list or order is stored here: the gate's children are the live
source of truth; a frozen copy goes stale. Fix dependencies surface only in
the commits, in hindsight. The 'human-reviewed' label is what separates review
rounds.

title: create-vm.md: restructure SSH key setup for local-first newcomers
description:
Current SSH Key Pair Setup section (lines 34-43) is cloud-first: immediately recommends setting up AWS first, even for users who only want to try local providers (Tart/Docker). Restructure to local-first:

1. Step 0 (everyone): generate a dedicated key with a non-default name to avoid collision with personal/GitHub keys. Recommended command:
   ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ansible_ed25519 -C "$(whoami)@$(hostname)"
   Explain: -f sets the filename; .pub extension is generated automatically; dedicated name keeps keys organised and grep-able. If you plan to reuse the key for AWS (which does not support ed25519), generate RSA or ECDSA instead and note this as a decision point.

2. Local providers (Tart/Docker): the generated key is sufficient — no external registration. Reference group_vars/tart/ and group_vars/docker/ for where to configure the public key.

3. Cloud providers: registration required per-provider. Existing links to prerequisites-aws.md / prerequisites-hcloud.md remain, reached after the key exists.

Goal: a newcomer who only wants to experiment locally can follow steps 0+2 with no cloud account.
close_reason: Closed

title: docs: replace -e with --extra-vars, combine into single quoted string
description:
All documentation files use -e (shorthand) for ansible-playbook extra-vars. Replace with --extra-vars throughout for new-user readability. Where multiple -e flags appear, combine into a single --extra-vars "key=val key2=val2" quoted string (canonical Ansible idiom; space-separated key=value pairs).

Do NOT add default-valued parameters to every example command — that bloats commands, hides which params are required vs optional, and creates hard-to-spot staleness when defaults change. Instead, document defaults in prose adjacent to the command (e.g. 'omit profile to use the basic default'). A single labeled 'full invocation' reference example is acceptable where one already exists or is clearly needed.

Scope: all .md files under docs/ and any quickstart/README files that contain ansible-playbook command examples.

title: Add opencode role with version-update integration
description:
Add Ansible role to install the OpenCode AI coding agent CLI as a system-wide binary at /usr/local/bin/opencode on Linux. Pins upstream release tag plus per-architecture SHA-256 of release tarballs. Integrates with playbooks/update-versions/{query,perform}-updates.yml so version + both sha256 pins refresh together. title: Create dedicated backup/restore doc, retire duplicated instructions
description:
docs/user-manual/work-with-vm.md and create-vm.md each inline backup/restore instructions independently and have drifted: both show bare 'ansible-playbook ./backup.yml' with no -e backup_from_host=<host> flag (now guaranteed to fail post-wlhi-fix), and work-with-vm.md links to inventories/group_vars/all/vars.yml as the place backup_from_host is configured (no longer true -- that var was removed from vars.yml in PR #39).

Fix: create a single combined doc docs/user-manual/backup-restore.md covering both backup.yml and restore.yml at aggregator-level depth (explain the backup_from_host / -e requirement once, link to playbooks/backup/ and playbooks/restore/ directories rather than enumerating each per-app playbook, so adding/removing an app playbook doesn't require a docs update).

Retrofit 4 touch points so the new doc is actually discoverable and the duplicated/stale instructions are removed:
1. New docs/user-manual/backup-restore.md (the doc itself).
2. docs/user-manual/work-with-vm.md: trim its Backup/Restore sections down to a pointer to the new doc; add nav footer 'Next: [Backup and Restore](./backup-restore.md)' (work-with-vm.md is currently the end of the Next:/Previous: chain, with no Next:).
3. docs/user-manual/backup-restore.md gets the matching 'Previous: [Work with a Virtual Machine](./work-with-vm.md)' footer to slot into that same linear nav chain.
4. README.md Quick Start bullet list: add an entry for the new doc, matching the existing 4-item list style.
5. docs/user-manual/create-vm.md: the inline backup command in its 'Delete the VM' section should point to the new doc instead of showing the bare (now-broken) command.

Run format-markdown on all touched/created Markdown files at close.
